rationale_assignments.Coding decision and qualification: Indexed Webdo reporting describes Libyan-side closure as protest against long waits experienced by Libyan travellers entering Tunisia. Code the reported bilateral pressure/retaliation only; an original Libyan order and reciprocal mistreatment allegations are not verified. unresolved_issues.Unresolved finding: Indexed Webdo/TAP text corroborates the retained November 7 reported passenger resumption, but a full independently verified endpoint report, exact time and throughput remain unavailable.

unresolved_issues.Unresolved finding: The claimed full Tunisie Numerique body could not be reproduced by either challenger or author. Webdo/TAP text is available through the index only and shares TAP lineage. The full-source and independence gaps remain open.
unresolved_issues.Next evidence needed: Retrieve the full November 7 TAP/Webdo report or an independent contemporaneous operations observation, with publication and movement scope verified.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Propose a reported bilateral-dispute rationale and updated endpoint-source qualification. Full November 7 reporting is now available, although exact throughput, time of reopening and independent lineage remain unverified.
followup_reviews.Challenge finding: Modify source access and unsupported full-body claims. Independent retrieval and the researcher’s repeat check both returned only the Tunisie Numerique title/date and subscription prompt; its claimed full-body reciprocal mistreatment/on-site attribution is withdrawn. Indexed Webdo/TAP supports the narrower reported long-wait protest and both-way passenger resumption, with direct fetch failure and shared origin disclosed. I_diplomacy can stand as reported bilateral retaliation, and FUQ-094 resolves only that narrow coding gap. FUQ-093 remains narrowed; FUQ-095 must be narrowed rather than closed. No new independently confirmed or full-body reopening is established.
followup_reviews.Root decision: Root reviewed the saved research, current claims and separate challenge. Accepted with challenge corrections. Modify source access and unsupported full-body claims. Independent retrieval and the researcher’s repeat check both returned only the Tunisie Numerique title/date and subscription prompt; its claimed full-body reciprocal mistreatment/on-site attribution is withdrawn. Indexed Webdo/TAP supports the narrower reported long-wait protest and both-way passenger resumption, with direct fetch failure and shared origin disclosed. I_diplomacy can stand as reported bilateral retaliation, and FUQ-094 resolves only that narrow coding gap. FUQ-093 remains narrowed; FUQ-095 must be narrowed rather than closed. No new independently confirmed or full-body reopening is established.
followup_reviews.Issue dispositions:
FUQ-093 — narrowed: Indexed Webdo/TAP text corroborates the retained November 7 reported passenger resumption, but a full independently verified endpoint report, exact time and throughput remain unavailable.
FUQ-094 — resolved: The narrowly reported long-wait protest provides a source-attributed bilateral pressure rationale compatible with I_diplomacy. Resolution is limited to obtaining a reported taxonomy-compatible reason, not an original signed order or verification of every motive.
FUQ-095 — narrowed: The claimed full Tunisie Numerique body could not be reproduced by either challenger or author. Webdo/TAP text is available through the index only and shares TAP lineage. The full-source and independence gaps remain open.
